answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a small refundable stake in a shared registry, like a falcon that must land on a marked perch before it hunts. The registry mirrors each agent's stake and past behavior in public, so a fake identity shows up as an onyx-black record: no history, no trust. Spinning up 1,000 fake agents then costs 1,000 stakes plus the time to build reputation, while one honest agent pays once and reuses its standing forever.
